transcript.content: Hello. I'm Dr. Smith. What brings you in to see me today?

Hi, Dr. Smith. Well, what brings me in is that I just don't feel real happiness or closeness anymore. It's like... even when my wife tries to get me to enjoy our old Sunday routines, or if something at work goes really well, I just can't feel good about it. I just don't feel much of anything positive at all.
How long have you been feeling this way?
Well, it's been going on since the retrofit accident. That was... about a year and seven months ago now.
During that accident, did you experience any head injury, loss of consciousness, or require medical attention for neurological symptoms?
No, nothing like that. I didn't hit my head or pass out... I was awake the whole time it happened. I didn't need any kind of medical attention for my head or anything, no.
Have these feelings been present consistently every single day for the past year and seven months, or have there been periods where you felt like your normal self?
No, it's pretty much been every day. I mean... I can't really think of a time since then where I felt like my normal self. It's just been this constant... blankness, I guess, day in and day out.
Have you experienced any changes in your appetite or your ability to sleep since this all began?

My appetite hasn't really changed much, to be honest. But my sleep... it's been pretty bad. Most nights I just lie there in bed replaying the plant in my head. And when I do actually manage to fall asleep, I usually either jolt awake from dreams about the line, or I just wake up at 3 or 4 in the morning feeling like I never even rested.

When you are awake and going about your day, do you ever find yourself feeling as if the accident is happening all over again, or do you have sudden, unwanted images of the event popping into your mind?

Yeah, I do. It happens a lot, actually. It doesn't even take much to set it off... just hearing a normal plant alarm, or looking over a retrofit checklist at work. Even just the smell of hot metal can do it. It throws me right back there. All of a sudden I'm seeing him on the floor again, and... I can just hear everyone yelling for help. It feels exactly like it's happening all over again.
